review_candidates.title: Senior Manager, People and Culture
review_candidates.description: The Role The Senior Manager, People and Culture is a new role, supporting a globally expanding team. The Senior Manager, People and Culture will lead two connected areas of GFC’s People and Culture strategy: Attract and Belong, and Reward and Retain. The role will oversee the employee experience from recruitment and onboarding through compensation, benefits, retention, and departure. It will design and manage fair, consistent people processes that reflect GFC’s values of courage, excellence, learning, partnership, and inclusion. This includes applying a DEIA lens to how GFC attracts and supports staff, recognizes contributions, makes decisions, and builds a sense of belonging across a globally distributed workforce. The Senior Manager will ensure that GFC’s people systems are both equitable and practical, with attention to different legal and employment contexts across countries. The role will advise managers on people matters, help them address issues with care and consistency, and support an employee experience where people are treated with respect and can contribute fully. This is a strategic and hands-on role. The Senior Manager will strengthen and manage core people systems, coordinate closely with colleagues across GFC, and oversee relationships with professional employer organizations and other external providers. Key Responsibilities: Attract and Belong • Lead GFC’s global recruitment approach, ensuring that hiring processes are equitable, inclusive, bias-aware, and consistent across teams and jurisdictions. • Manage recruitment processes from role scoping and job description development through advertising, shortlisting, interviews, selection, offers, and pre-employment checks. • Assist in offer negotiations; prepare employment offers and contracts, aligned with regulatory compliance and internal equity • Advise hiring managers on recruitment strategy, selection criteria, interview design, candidate assessment, and equitable decision-making. • Strengthen GFC’s employee value proposition so candidates receive a clear and honest picture of the organization, its culture, and its expectations. • Develop sourcing and outreach approaches that attract strong and diverse candidate pools across GFC’s global footprint. • Monitor recruitment data, including diversity of candidate pools, time to hire, offer acceptance, and candidate experience, and use the findings to improve GFC’s practices. • Lead a consistent and welcoming global onboarding process, working with managers and colleagues across functions to ensure new staff have the relationships, information, systems, and clarity they need to succeed. • Establish clear responsibilities and checkpoints for managers during recruitment, onboarding, probation, and confirmation. Build manager capability in these areas through practical guidance, coaching, and tools that support a positive and consistent employee experience. • Gather feedback from new employees and hiring managers and use it to strengthen recruitment and onboarding. • Support practices that build belonging from the beginning of an employee’s experience at GFC. Reward and Retain • Coordinate GFC’s approach to compensation and benefits across its countries of operation, supporting fair and transparent decisions while accounting for local legal requirements and employment practices. • Manage annual compensation review processes, including planning, guidance, documentation, internal equity analysis, and coordination with Finance and senior leadership. • Support the development and implementation of GFC’s reward philosophy, salary structures, job levels, benchmarking approach, and recognition practices. • Maintain accurate information about salaries, benefits, employment arrangements, and contractual requirements across jurisdictions. • Review market data and internal comparisons to identify pay gaps, compression, inconsistencies, and retention risks. • Advise managers and leaders on promotions, salary adjustments, benefits, employment changes, and other reward decisions. • Ensure that salary and employment decisions are properly documented, approved, communicated, and implemented. • Coordinate global benefits reviews and renewals in partnership with Finance, brokers, PEOs, and other providers. • Track retention, turnover, exit themes, critical roles, and other workforce trends, and recommend practical action in response. • Work with senior leaders to identify capability gaps, talent risks, and future workforce needs, and support workforce planning, talent management, and succession planning for critical roles. • Oversee consistent and respectful offboarding processes, including documentation, handovers, exit feedback, and coordination with relevant internal and external partners. Global People Operations and PEO Management • Serve as the primary relationship manager for GFC’s professional employer organizations and relevant employment service providers. • Monitor provider performance, service quality, costs, response times, contractual commitments, and resolution of employee issues. • Coordinate employment contracts, contract changes, payroll instructions, benefits administration, leave arrangements, and employee departures across PEO-supported jurisdictions. • Work with providers and internal colleagues to ensure employment practices comply with applicable local requirements. • Maintain clear records of employment arrangements, statutory obligations, benefits, notice periods, and other jurisdiction-specific requirements. • Identify operational or compliance risks and escalate them promptly, seeking specialist legal advice where required. • Develop clear processes, guidance, templates, and service standards so staff and managers understand how people-related requests and decisions are handled. • Maintain accurate, secure, and accessible people data in accordance with data protection requirements. • Manage GFC’s HR systems, including day-to-day administration, data quality, regular people reporting, and continuous improvement of systems and workflows in partnership with relevant colleagues and providers. • Work closely with Finance to reconcile payroll and benefits information and ensure approved changes are implemented accurately and on time. Partnership and Organizational Contribution • Build trusted working relationships with staff, managers, senior leaders, Finance, Operations, and other teams. • Provide sound, practical advice while applying policies and principles consistently. • Contribute to the implementation and continued development of GFC’s People and Culture strategy. • Use workforce data and staff feedback to identify patterns, risks, and opportunities for improvement. • Analyze workforce data and staff feedback to identify barriers to inclusion, progression, and retention, and recommend action to improve equity and the employee experience. • Support organizational change by ensuring that its implications for recruitment, employment arrangements, reward, retention, and the employee experience are properly considered. • Model GFC’s commitment to trust, candor, shared power, learning, care, transparency, and accountability. Essential Experience and Knowledge • Proficiency in HR analytics and evidence-based decision making with targeted experience in HRIS systems implementation and administration • Significant experience in a people and culture or human resources role, including responsibility for both recruitment and reward or people operations. • Experience managing recruitment and onboarding processes from beginning to end. • Experience coordinating compensation reviews, salary benchmarking, benefits, or related reward processes. • Experience supporting employees across more than one country or employment jurisdiction within a global framework, employing team members across many countries and jurisdictions • Experience managing PEOs, employers of record, benefits providers, brokers, or comparable external employment partners. • Strong working knowledge of equitable and inclusive recruitment practices. • Experience developing and improving people processes, guidance, templates, and systems during periods of organizational change. • Experience working in a fast-paced, evolving organization, adapting priorities while maintaining consistent people processes and support. • Ability to interpret people data, identify risks and patterns, and translate findings into practical recommendations. • Sound judgment and a clear understanding of confidentiality and responsible handling of employee information. • Strong project management skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple processes, deadlines, and stakeholders. • Clear and thoughtful written and verbal communication skills. • Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, shared power, and GFC’s values. Desirable Experience • Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible human resource experience, ideally within a matrixed, and global organization with experience at international non-profits. • Knowledge of employment practices in the United States, United Kingdom, or other countries where GFC employs staff. • Experience contributing to job architecture, salary structures, or a global reward framework. • Experience with HR information systems, applicant tracking systems, or performance and compensation platforms. • Experience supporting organizational restructuring or other significant change processes. • A relevant professional certificatoin or equivalent experience in human resources or people management. Approach to the Role The successful candidate will combine attention to detail with sound judgment. They will be comfortable building structure where processes are still developing, holding colleagues accountable for agreed actions, and adapting global principles to different local contexts. They will communicate directly, treat employees with care, and follow through reliably. Reporting and Working Relationships The Senior Manager, People and Culture will report to the Senior Advisor, People and Culture. The role will work closely with the People and Culture team, Safeguarding, Finance, Operations, managers across GFC, and external employment and benefits providers. The role may manage staff, consultants, or project support as the People and Culture function develops. Location GFC is a globally distributed organization, with most of the team working remotely. Candidates may apply from any location, provided they can maintain regular working-hour overlap with colleagues in both US Eastern and UK time zones and adjust their schedules as needed. Candidates based in the UK or US are eligible for direct employment. Candidates based elsewhere will be engaged through a PEO/EOR arrangement. What can we oﬀer you? Our team dreams big. We work together to build a world where all children and youth are safe, strong and valued. GFC fosters a caring work environment that promotes collaboration, respect, and professional development. We set standards of excellence and quality in our work, ﬁrmly believing that children and youth deserve the best we can oﬀer. We believe that every person has equal rights, and we aﬃrm the diversity that enriches our globalized world. In line with these core values, it is our policy to actively seek diverse candidates from a variety of backgrounds who are committed to Global Fund for Children’s mission. Our values shape our vision, guide our daily decision making, and signal to the world what to expect when you encounter Global Fund for Children. We hold ourselves to these values to best serve our local partners and the children and youth they support. We attract talented people from all over the world because we believe deeply in living our values. Salary Range – For US-based candidates, the salary range is $85,000 to $110,000 dependent on level of experience. International hires will be locally benchmarked dependent on location, available benefits, and experience. Learning – GFC encourages professional development as a part of our culture and values. GFC provides regular opportunities for training, collaboration, and mentorship. Employees may access professional development funds to support continued learning. Beneﬁts - We strive to build a culture that embraces care and wellbeing. Our global employee beneﬁts include: • Private healthcare insurance plan with comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage • Generous paid time oﬀ (annual leave, enhanced sickness leave, wellbeing days, sabbatical leave, family friendly leave) • Flexible work arrangements - remote/hybrid/compressed work schedules • Pension contributions • Employee Assistance Services • Team Building and Social Committees *Other beneﬁts may apply, depending on the location of the employee To Apply Please submit a resume/CV and a brief cover letter explaining your interest and relevant qualifications. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. How do I apply? In line with our values of courage, passion and inclusion, to apply for this role, please share your thoughts on the following questions along with your CV through the following link: https://global-fund-for-children.breezy.hr/p/e4bba9e3acd9 Please keep each answer to 200 words or fewer 1) What most excites you about this role? 2) Briefly summarize your relevant experience and expertise. Include specific examples of HR issues you have handled, your role in addressing them, and the impact of your approach. 3) Which parts of this role are you most excited to dig into, even if they may be complex, and how would you bring curiosity and care to that work? 4) If selected, when would you be able to start a new position? The deadline for applications is Monday, November 30, 2026 at 5pm US Eastern Time. We are excited to hear from you if you have any questions about the role, please get in touch on careers@globalfundforchildren.org

review_candidates.description: About the MicroBuild Initiative: The MicroBuild Initiative is a cornerstone of Habitat’s impact strategy over the next decade. The MicroBuild Initiative builds on the success of MicroBuild Fund 1, which leveraged $100 million to catalyze more than $1.2 billion in affordable housing finance for almost 240,000 families across 33 countries since 2012. As part of the MicroBuild Initiative, the second fund is expected to be significantly larger — in the range of $300 million to $500 million. Alongside the Fund, the initiative will be comprised of the Impact & Innovation Hub which will deliver technical assistance, innovation, and advocacy to help transform housing systems globally. The initiative aims to directly benefit more than 2.5 million people in emerging and developing economies as they work to improve their homes. About the Role: The Senior Director, Technical Assistance & Innovation reports to the Managing Director, MicroBuild Initiative Impact & Innovation Hub and is responsible for the design, coordination, delivery, quality assurance, and performance management of all technical assistance delivered through the Hub. The position is responsible for ensuring that the specific capacity building needs of MicroBuild Fund 2 investees are met. Services may include but not be limited to housing readiness assessments, product development support, and other investee capacity-building. The role serves as the primary operational bridge between the Hub and the Housing Finance Systems (HFS) team within Habitat's Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter (TCIS) and is accountable for ensuring technical assistance activities contribute to stronger institutional performance, achievement of Fund objectives, and fulfillment of Habitat's commitments to the MicroBuild Initiative. The Senior Director works closely with the Managing Director, MicroBuild Impact & Innovation Hub, TCIS and HFS leadership, technical specialists, consultants, and external partners to ensure technical assistance assignments and TA innovations generate measurable results, institutional learning, and scalable market impact. During the initial years of Fund implementation, the Sr. Director is expected to oversee and coordinate a portfolio of approximately 15-30 technical assistance engagements annually, requiring effective portfolio management, technical resource coordination, consultant oversight, performance monitoring, and close collaboration with internal and external partners. The incumbent will play a key role in identifying, informing, and supporting Technical Assistance (TA) innovation to achieve more efficient and effective TA delivery that delivers sustained results at institutional and systems levels. Leveraging insights from MicroBuild 1 (MB1) TA feedback and from new MicroBuild TA delivery, and working closely with the Director, Global Program Design and Execution - HFS, the incumbent will participate in the development and oversight of 2–3 TA innovation pilots annually designed to benefit multiple institutions and advance the broader housing finance market. This position may be based in Washington, DC, Nairobi, Kenya, London, United Kingdom, or San Jose, Costa Rica and follows a hybrid work arrangement, requiring a combination of in-office and remote work with up to 40% international travel. Key Responsibilities: 1. Technical Assistance Strategy, Delivery & Portfolio Management – 40% Develop and implement the Hub's technical assistance strategy and tools Manage the overall technical assistance portfolio and annual workplan. Align technical assistance priorities with annual Fund pipeline plans and emerging institutional needs. Participate in annual and other periodic pipeline planning discussions with the Hub Managing Director, Symbiotics, Senior Director HFS, and other relevant stakeholders. Oversee the full lifecycle of technical assistance engagements, from identification and design through implementation and close-out. Manage technical assistance budgets, timelines, risks, resource requirements, and performance expectations. Ensure technical assistance resources are allocated efficiently across institutions and markets. Monitor portfolio performance and recommend adjustments based on evolving needs, lessons learned, and Fund priorities. 2. Consultant & Partner Management – 20% Build and manage a network of consultants, advisors, and implementation partners. Coordinate internal and external technical resources to support delivery of high-quality services. Support development of scopes of work, procurement processes, and engagement strategies. Oversee consultant performance and quality of deliverables. Support contracting, budgeting, and resource planning related to technical assistance delivery. Support transfer of lessons learned from Fund-supported institutions into TCIS programs, tools, and broader housing finance initiatives. 3. Learning & Knowledge Management – 15% Drive continuous improvement of the Hub's technical assistance and innovation approaches by incorporating field experience, implementation evidence, investee feedback, and lessons learned into technical methodologies, tools, and delivery models, while contributing to the ongoing development of Habitat's housing finance advisory capabilities Contribute to annual country housing finance analyses and learning products. Support evaluation and documentation of innovative approaches and solutions. Contribute technical expertise to joint Hub-TCIS innovation and market development initiatives. Support development of learning papers, case studies, toolkits, conference presentations, and thought leadership materials. Promote application of lessons learned across the technical assistance portfolio. 4. Impact Measurement & Reporting – 15% Work closely with the Research and Learning (MEARL) Manager to establish and monitor technical assistance performance indicators. Track institutional, portfolio-level, and market-level outcomes resulting from technical assistance delivery. Evaluate effectiveness, scalability, and impact of technical assistance and innovation interventions. Contribute to annual reporting and Fund reporting processes. Provide analysis of program and service effectiveness, lessons learned, institutional outcomes, and portfolio trends. Support evidence-based decision making regarding future technical assistance and innovation investments and priorities. Contribute information and analysis required for Board reporting, annual reports, stakeholder communications, and Fund reporting requirements. 5. Innovation Catalyst – 10% Collaborate with TCIS and other stakeholders to conceptualize, design, and implement pilots focused on innovations in housing finance that can be applied across multiple institutions and geographies. Partner with TCIS, financial institutions, external partners, and other HFHI stakeholders to co-create solutions that address emerging market needs and opportunities. Coordinate engagement with external partners to support innovation initiatives and pilot implementation. Key Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, International Development, Public Policy, Housing, or a related field required. Minimum 12 years of progressively responsible experience providing technical assistance and capacity-building support to financial institutions (including banks, microfinance institutions, community lenders, and other emerging financial intermediaries) in emerging and developing markets. Demonstrated expertise in assessing institutional capacity; designing and delivering technical assistance programs that strengthen housing finance and lending operations, design new products; and building relationships with financial institution partners across regions. Experience working in developing and emerging economies, with a proven ability to build and manage relationships with people and organizations across cultures. Proven track record managing multi-country technical assistance portfolios, including strategy development, work planning, budgeting, implementation oversight, quality assurance, and performance improvement. Experience working directly with financial institutions to assess organizational capacity, identify performance gaps, and implement operational, financial, product, and risk management improvements. Experience facilitating collaboration across cross-functional teams, including program, finance, legal, compliance, monitoring and evaluation, MEARL and communications.

review_candidates.description: Actualités Avis & Communiqués Offres d'Emploi Publireportage SOS Villages d’Enfants Guinée recrute un (e) Directeur (trice) de programme : annonce Par admin 23 juillet 2016 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Fondée en 1949, SOS Villages d’Enfants International est une Organisation Internationale de développement social qui œuvre dans plus de 132 pays à travers le monde, dans le but de satisfaire les besoins et de protéger les droits des enfants vulnérables. Tout en axant son travail sur les enfants qui ne bénéficient pas de l’éducation parentale ou encore les enfants en difficulté dans diverses circonstances, l’organisation a développé plusieurs programmes notamment : les villages d’enfants, les centres pour jeunes, les programmes d’appui à la famille, des écoles et crèches, des centres d’apprentissage et des centres de santé mère-enfant dans chaque pays où elle déploie ses activités. SOS Villages d’Enfants est implantée en République de Guinée depuis 1989 (zones d’intervention : Conakry, Kankan, N’Zérékoré, Labé), et dépend administrativement du Bureau International Région Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre basé à Dakar. Dans le cadre de sa planification stratégique, SOS Villages d’Enfants Guinée lance le recrutement de trois Directeurs/trices de Programme pour les sites de Conakry, N’zérékoré et Kankan. Voir plus Nouvelles Guinée Actualités Guinée Voyages Guinée Missions Placé sous la supervision directe du Directeur National (DN), le/la Directeur(trice) de Programme des Villages d’Enfants SOS (DPVE) assure avec l’appui et le suivi du personnel du bureau national, le développement et la mise en œuvre globale du programme des Villages d’Enfants SOS, afin de répondre aux besoins des sites, conformément à la vision, à la mission, à la stratégie, et aux normes de l’organisation. Il/elle représente l’organisation auprès des parties prenantes gouvernementales et non-gouvernementales au niveau des sites. Il/elle coordonne les activités du Programme Villages d’Enfant (PVE) et les interventions et assure la qualité et l’efficacité des services ainsi que leur rapport qualité/coût grâce à l’assurance qualité et l’utilisation optimale des ressources. Le DPVE est responsable de la mise en œuvre de la gestion du cycle de programme dans le site assurant ainsi que le PVE est adapté à la situation locale et contribue à l’élaboration d’un système social durable pour le groupe cible. Il/elle dirige et supervise la gestion des collègues de différents services au sein du programme, y compris le travail spécialisé avec différentes formes de familles ainsi que les travaux de soutien d’ordre général. Il/elle identifie les sources de revenus potentiels en collaboration avec le Département Collecte de Fonds et Communications du Bureau National et/ou de la Direction Nationale. En tant que membre de l’Équipe Nationale de gestion il/elle participe à la planification annuelle et stratégique de l’association membre. {0> Strategic planning: Qualifications : Master en management, gestion des entreprises, gestion de projets, ou en sciences économiques. Un diplôme d’études supérieures supplémentaire dans l’un des domaines suivants serait un atout : Gestion des Ressources Humaines, Psychologie, Psycho-sociale, Education, Développement de services de la jeunesse, et développement communautaire ou travail social) ; Au moins 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle en matière de Management et encadrement de qualité des Jeunes/ Enfants (de préférence dans des ONG locales, nationales ou internationales) ; Une solide expérience dans l’encadrement/l’éducation des jeunes, le travail social ou le développement communautaire est souhaitable ; Une expérience dans le développement de l’enfant, les droits et la protection de l’enfant est une exigence ; Parfaite maîtrise du français et bonne connaissance de l’anglais ; Bonne maîtrise du pack office ; Disponibilité à voyager à l’intérieur et à l’extérieur du pays. Aptitudes Agir en tant que modèle (les comportements et les opinions servant de point de référence) ; Réflexion stratégique et innovante (penser et d’agir d’une manière visionnaire et stratégique) ; Vivre et promouvoir la diversité ; Capacités de communication, de négociation et d’interaction ; Orientation de la performance ; Capacité de gestion des conflits et des situations d’urgence ; Capacité à conseiller et à coacher ; Honnêteté et éthique ; Innovation, créativité, flexibilité et prise d’initiatives ; Proactivité et capacité de s’adapter au changement ; Forte capacité de planification, d’organisation, de résolution de problèmes et de prise de décisions. Capacité de gestion du temps. Aptitude prouvée à définir une direction stratégique claire, à motiver les collaborateurs et à créer des opportunités pour leur développement. Nous Offrons Un salaire et des avantages compétitifs. Un environnement de travail stimulant. L’opportunité de travailler pour une ONG internationale reconnue et respectée Conditions Du Poste Etre de nationalité guinéenne Date de prise de fonction : immédiate Nb Les candidat(e)s doivent adresser au Directeur National de SOS Village d’Enfants Guinée : une lettre de motivation, en indiquant le site souhaité : Conakry, Kankan ou Nzérékoré. un curriculum vitae, une copie des diplômes et des attestations des expériences dans les domaines couverts par le poste (stages, formations etc.), la liste de trois personnes de référence avec leur adresse complète. Les dossiers susmentionnés devront être envoyés aux adresses électroniques suivantes : Ressources.Humaines@sosguinea.org et sos-no@sosguinea.org avec en objet la mention : Candidature au poste SOS/DP/2016 La date limite de réception des dossiers est fixée au 10/08/2016 Les dossiers de candidature incomplets et non-conformes au profil recherché ne seront pas examinés.
